claim: KIIS conducted a representative all-Ukrainian telephone survey on 3-11 December 2021 specifically measuring trust in social institutions, providing a contemporaneous population-level sensor for institutional confidence before the invasion.
limitations: The searchable source confirms survey design and timing; exact institution-by-institution values should be imported only after reliable extraction of the full table. Occupied territories were excluded.

claim: KIIS survey on 13-16 December 2021 found 49.2% of respondents considered a Russian invasion threat real while 41.4% believed there would be no invasion.
limitations: Population perception is not evidence that invasion was objectively certain. Survey excludes Crimea and non-government-controlled parts of Donetsk/Luhansk.

claim: The same KIIS survey reported 57.8% considered government diplomatic and defense efforts to prevent a full-scale invasion insufficient, while 27.1% considered them sufficient.
limitations: Measures perceived confidence in the response, not actual preparedness or causal propensity toward conflict.

claim: KIIS December 2021 polling found national majorities favored EU and NATO accession, while support was stronger in West/Centre and lower in South/East; for NATO in South/East, support and opposition were approximately evenly divided.
limitations: Geopolitical orientation is not identical to ethnic/language identity or conflict disposition; regional aggregate differences must not be essentialized.

claim: World Bank Systematic Country Diagnostic consultations in September 2021 described persistent and pervasive institutional weaknesses as a major constraint on growth, public-service delivery and job creation in Ukraine.
limitations: Development diagnosis is broad structural evidence, not a direct measure of conflict risk or public legitimacy.

claim: World Bank reporting in April-May 2021 documented both COVID-related learning-loss/inequality risks and a $200 million higher-education modernization project supporting digital infrastructure, resilience and learning continuity.
limitations: Program approval demonstrates counter-pressure and capacity-building, not proof that inequality or learning loss was reversed by a given cutoff.
